messages:
Marta Kolodziej: heads up — we're planning a canary for model v3.2 next week. want to settle on a percent-ramp + guard semantics for the console/API. thinking: small initial step (1%), then 5%, 25%, 50%, 100% with automatic backoff on p95/error spikes. any objections?

Jon Park: sounds reasonable. i worry about models with variable latency profiles — p95 can jump with a single noisy tenant. we should allow a rolling window and an absolute tolerance (eg, baseline_p95 * 1.25 or +50ms) not just absolute thresholds.

Lia Gomez: agree with jon. also UX ask: expose a preview graph in the console that shows traffic over time with estimated token cost delta per step. PMs want to see dollars before they hit start. :money_with_wings:

Kevin Liu: API debate: do we encode schedule as an explicit list of steps or as a ramp object (start, end, duration, granularity)? i prefer explicit steps for predictable guard checks and auditability. sample YAML below: 
```yaml
canary:
  steps:
    - percent: 1
      duration: 30m
      guards:
        p95_latency_ms: 200
        error_rate_pct: 0.5
    - percent: 5
      duration: 1h
    - percent: 25
      duration: 2h
    - percent: 50
      duration: 4h
    - percent: 100
      duration: 0h
  backoff_policy:
    max_retries: 2
    cool_off: 30m
  fast_forward: true  # manual operator can fast-forward
```

Lia Gomez: that YAML looks fine. +1 for explicit steps. also suggest adding `slo_window` and `trigger_window` so guards evaluate on the right buckets (eg, 5m trigger, 30m slo).

Kevin Liu: +1 to window params. one more: we need to decide whether guards are evaluated per-route or globally across the whole model. some customers route different tenants to same model; per-route makes smaller blasts but more noisy. default should be global unless route filter provided.

Marta Kolodziej: excellent points. for defaults i'd prefer global guards to protect infra, and allow `route_filters` opt-in for tenant-aware rollouts. ops and SRE can override per-customer.

Ops QA: deploy-bot should emit a canary-summary event with resolved baselines and current capacity targets. makes it easier to correlate with traces. also add a `reason` field to every step change (manual or auto).

Jon Park: one operational edge-case: what if backoff triggers at 25% and we don't have capacity to retry smaller step (because 5% instances were scaled down)? need a guard that ensures minimum capacity is kept during canary (pin hosts or min_instances).

Marta Kolodziej: good catch. add `min_reserved_instances` and `min_capacity_pct` as part of canary config. i'll sketch that in the API.

Kevin Liu: final API thought — return a clear rollout_status object in the public API with fields: current_step, percent, reason, last_guard_eval, next_step_eta. makes frontend and automation consistent.

Lia Gomez: UX note: console should surface an explict "pause" button when a guard trips, with suggested remediation (increase capacity, rollback, or extend slo_window).

deploy-bot: CANARY INITIATED for model v3.2 by marta@redwood — step 1 at 1% scheduled. (this is a staged thread test message)

Marta Kolodziej: action items: 1) kevin will draft the API shape for explicit-steps + windows + backoff (kevin:+2d) 2) lia will design the preview graph and pause UX (lia:+3d) 3) jon/ops QA to write SRE playbook for min_capacity and rollback (jon/ops QA:+4d). ping me when PRs land. :thumbsup:
